findings.title: Shared AsyncStorage keys can expose previous account's applied/rejected shift markers after account switching.
findings.scenario: Sara uses a shared phone and marks shift IDs applied or rejected; after logout Tom signs in on the same device. The shift board persistence hook hydrates applied/rejected marker IDs from device-global AsyncStorage keys without an account prefix. Tom can briefly see Sara's state as his own until backend data refresh and shift pruning.
findings.test_needed: Native shared device: Sara applies/rejects shifts, signs out; Tom signs in and opens community board with slow server results. Assert applied/rejected markers never display Sara's state, and subsequent writes are isolated. Check default disableLocalPersistence behavior and whether backend props override early hydration.
